title: Getting started
markdown:
## A small device. A familiar companion.
Pika records your thoughts with a physical button. Pika Companion on Android keeps your library, connects to online services and lets you continue Ask without the device.

## What you need
- A supported Pika ESP32-S3 e-paper device with a working microSD card and the matching V8 firmware.
- Pika Companion for Android 8 or later. Enable Bluetooth and grant the permissions Android requests. Older Android versions may also require Location for Bluetooth discovery.
- Your own OpenAI API key and internet on the phone for recognition, AI and voice responses. Provider usage may incur charges; a ChatGPT subscription is separate.

## First pairing
1. Wake Pika with the lower button and open Companion. Choose Get started, then Find Pika.
2. Select your Pika and confirm the pairing code shown on its screen. The short PN serial identifies the device; it is not the pairing code.
3. Complete setup: OpenAI key is required, then choose a voice. Male · Cedar is the default.
4. Optionally connect Calendar and Gmail, choose a theme and set a four-digit application PIN. Light is the default theme.
5. If the app closes before setup finishes, open it again. The saved pairing is kept and setup resumes. A missing API key returns you to the required key step.

## Your first memory
Hold the upper button, speak, then release. This saves a memory, even if you mention work or appointments. Ask is where you request tasks and events. Recordings shorter than half a second are discarded as accidental presses.

## Your first Ask
Hold the lower button, speak, then release. Try: “What memories do I have?” or “Create a task to call Alex tomorrow by 2 pm.” You can also type or hold the microphone in the app's Ask tab. Use Russian or English naturally.

## Keep the companion available
Allow Bluetooth and background operation for Companion in Android settings. If your phone aggressively limits background apps, allow unrestricted battery use for Companion. The device advertises while awake; reconnection and queued transfers resume when the phone is available. Pika sleeps to save battery, so an offline phone edit may wait until its next wake.

title: Everyday use
markdown:
## Today and navigation
Today shows active memories, open tasks and events for today / upcoming events. Completed tasks are not counted as open. Mail appears when configured. Tap the counters on the app illustration to open their sections. Battery percentage, voltage and SD free / total space appear in the top status panel.

Use the bottom icons for Today, Memories, Tasks, Events, Ask and Config. Swipe horizontally to move between main sections; reverse an unfinished swipe to cancel it. Archive and Calendar are available in Config. The calendar icon beside a list heading opens Calendar. Android Back closes a dialog first; otherwise it returns to Today.

## Physical controls
Default actions on Today:
- Upper single: tasks. Upper double: daily briefing. Upper hold: record memory. Upper triple: no action.
- Lower single: events. Lower double: weekly briefing. Lower hold: Ask. Lower triple: clock.
- Hold both buttons to request a companion reconnection. This is not a local Wi-Fi web-server command in V8.

Change single, double, triple and hold assignments in Config → Home button actions. Record and Ask are offered on hold slots. Inside an active screen, that screen's controls take over; Today combinations resume after returning home. The month calendar and weather close with either button. Lower / Back stops Mail narration and leaves Mail. Clock stays awake until exited; the other extra screens return to Today before timed sleep.

## Memories
Memories contain your original recording and transcript. Edit the transcript to correct recognition; it stays a memory. In the app, Add memory offers a pencil for text or a microphone for hold-to-record. Voice notes are kept for later processing if internet is unavailable. Manually editing an untranscribed note prevents automatic recognition from overwriting your text.

Copy copies the transcript. Share opens Android sharing with the transcript and WAV when available. TXT and WAV downloads are also offered in the editor. Forget archives a memory and removes its WAV; restoring it brings back text only. A complete earlier backup may still contain the old recording.

## Tasks, events and archives
Tasks support priority and an optional deadline. No deadline means the task stays open until you complete or archive it. Events support a start/end, all-day dates and multi-day spans. Past events remain on their calendar dates and appear in Archive; they are not automatically erased.

Archive search matches titles, full text and related fields across dates. Archived task and memory lists show the newest archive changes first, with 24 items per page. Archive's trash action permanently deletes all archived data after confirmation. Undo and restore depend on retained recovery copies; keep a full backup before destructive cleanup.

## Sleep and offline operation
The inverted Today screen indicates sleep; waking returns to the light device screen. The inactivity timer follows Device & controls. Queued background processing and empty sync checks do not add extra idle time; an active transfer may finish before sleep. On the app, the sleeping illustration is dimmed. The activity LED, when enabled, indicates work or communication; the red charging indicator is independent.

Without the phone, Pika still records memories and queues them. With the phone but no internet, recordings wait for recognition. Offline Ask recordings can be transferred later: actionable requests are handled in capture order; ordinary conversational questions are skipped. Weather and Mail keep cached information after a failed refresh. Ask and live service screens may show No connection or Try again when their dependencies are unavailable.

## Voice memories on your phone
In Memories, choose Add memory → microphone. Tap once to record hands-free; tap Stop to save. Android keeps the screen on while recording. You can create the next memory while earlier WAV files and transcripts synchronize in the background. Recordings shorter than half a second are discarded.

Pull down to recheck the awake device and pending changes. Repeated pulls during an active exchange do not queue duplicate synchronization passes. A sleeping device is not woken remotely. A small sync icon beside a memory stays still while queued and rotates only while that specific recording is being sent. It disappears when Pika confirms reception.

title: Ask companion
markdown:
## One conversation, on both sides
Ask combines general questions, web search, your active records and read-only mail. The phone can send typed or spoken questions without Pika nearby. Long-press a message bubble to copy it. The conversation opens at its latest messages; date dividers help you find older exchanges.

History is retained, but model context is bounded: do not treat every old message as permanently present in each request. Renew starts a clean conversation using current personal records. It does not delete the records themselves. Full backups include the dialogue and available device context/history files.

## Keep notes as notes
Upper-button recording always creates a memory. To turn a memory into a plan, use Ask and identify the note by its subject, a phrase from it, when it was captured or “the latest memory.” When similar memories exist, ask for a summary first and clarify the one you mean.

## Useful requests
- “Create tasks and events from my latest memory about the website.”
- “Create a high-priority task to send the files by Friday at 2 pm.”
- “Create an event tomorrow at 7:30 pm for one hour.”
- “Create an all-day event from November 5 to November 8.”
- “Mark the task about the TV remote as completed.”
- “Cancel all events tomorrow about the workshop.”
- “Restore the task about homework from the archive.”
- “Look in the archive for the memory about my trip.”
- “Преврати последнюю заметку о сайте в задачи и события.”
- “Пометь задачу про пульт как выполненную.”

Relative dates use the capture/request date in Europe/Kyiv. Tasks without a requested deadline remain undated. Give a time or duration when it matters. Ambiguous requests may need clarification; check the resulting records after a batch operation.

## Changes and archive scope
Config → Ask companion controls voice changes to existing records. Enable Allow voice changes to records for edit, complete, archive and restore workflows. Normal questions use active records; mention archive explicitly when you want historical data. Deleting a task through Ask means completing/archiving it in the record workflow, not purging its history. Permanent archive deletion is a separate confirmed action.

## Mail and web
Ask can fetch your configured filtered mail. Try “Read my unread mail briefly.” Summaries aim for sender, subject and message, replacing links rather than speaking long URLs. Mail access is read only. General current-information questions can use web search; availability depends on phone internet, credentials and the provider. Source links appear with answers when returned.

## When an action fails
A failed or ambiguous plan should not be treated as completed. Check the records before repeating a create request. If a response says Try again, inspect Config → Diagnostics for the cause, check internet/API access, then retry. The device and app keep bounded error journals with up to 200 entries.

title: Fine-tune your Pika
markdown:
## AI and voice
Config → AI & voice changes your OpenAI key and reply voice. Leave a saved-key field empty to retain the key. Cedar is male; Coral is female. Answers follow Russian or English questions. A saved key is not a guarantee that the provider account has usable billing, quota or access.

## Buttons and extra screens
Assign actions independently for upper/lower single, double, triple and hold. Use original defaults resets the mapping. Assign Weather, Month calendar or Mail to a combination if you want it on the device. Weather is refreshed when opening Weather. Mail is refreshed when opening Mail rather than on every wake. The device does not need saved Wi-Fi networks in the phone-companion mode; internet services run through the phone.

## Sleep timer
Config → Device & controls → Sleep timer sets 1–5 minutes of inactivity (default: 1 minute). Save to queue the setting for Pika; it applies when connected and survives restart. Active recording and synchronization finish safely before sleep. Clock remains visible. Complete backups include this device setting; restore with Pika connected to apply it again.

## Sound, reminders and activity light
Sound & melody controls speaker volume, reminder melody and per-scenario notification patterns. Choose No sound for any scenario you want silent. Patterns cover recording start, successful Ask, saved memory, errors / no connection, increased unread mail, wake readiness and sleep. Use the separate Test on Pika selector to preview a melody on the connected device. A disconnected or sleeping Pika cannot play a live test.

Event reminders live in the sound section. Enable them, set minutes before a timed event and alert duration. Cached events allow device reminders without a live internet connection. Lower / Back stops an alert. All-day events are not timed reminders. Confirm the device clock, volume and reminder settings with a short test event before relying on alerts.

The optional activity LED lights while recording or communicating and turns off when idle/ready. It does not control the hardware charging LED.

## Appearance and access
Choose light or dark theme in Config. The optional four-digit PIN locks only the app; it is separate from Bluetooth pairing. Five quick taps on the Today case illustration open its colors. Use the continuous palette or a HEX value for the body and buttons. Default returns the original SVG colors. Both awake and sleeping illustrations share the palette; sleep retains its dimming.

## Sync and status
Pull down from the top to request sync. The thin orange bar and status text show progress. Ordinary sync exchanges changes; Force full sync in Config verifies the whole library. Library edits on the phone are saved locally immediately, then queued for Pika. During a full restore, the device illustration shows RESTORING and dashes until activation is acknowledged.

## Google Calendar
1. Enable Calendar API in your Google Cloud project. Create a service account and download its JSON key.
2. Share the target Google calendar with that JSON's client_email and allow event changes.
3. In Google Calendar settings, copy the explicit Calendar ID under Integrate calendar. Do not use “primary” for the service account.
4. In Config → Google Calendar, choose the key, enter the ID and save. Test the connection / import with Pika connected if requested by the app.

Local event changes are exported to Google. Import missing Google events is a separate action. Edits to an already imported event in Google are not a general two-way merge in this version. Configured means credentials are present; verify a real operation before assuming access works.

## Gmail
1. Enable Gmail API. Configure OAuth consent and add your account as a test user if the Google project is in Testing.
2. Create an OAuth client of type Desktop app. On your computer save its JSON as config/gmail-oauth-client.json in the source checkout you use.
3. Run python tools/gmail_connect.py from that checkout, sign in and grant read-only mail access.
4. Import the generated config/gmail-account.json in Config → Gmail, then save.

Up to four filters accept an exact sender address or a domain such as @example.com. Mail shows up to four recent unread incoming conversations from the last seven days. Empty filters use Inbox / Primary. Spam, Trash, drafts and your own replies are excluded. Reading does not mark mail read. Only the latest incoming content in a conversation is used. Testing-mode Google authorizations can expire; reconnect when Google rejects a token.

## Weather
Set one location name and latitude/longitude in Config. Assign Weather to a device combination. Opening the screen requests fresh Open-Meteo data through the phone; failures retain the saved forecast and its timestamp. The screen includes current conditions, high/low and upcoming forecast slots. Dates use Europe/Kyiv.

## Wi-Fi boost
Under Device & controls, enable Wi-Fi boost and enter a reachable 2.4 GHz network name and password once. Android cannot retrieve saved Wi-Fi passwords for sharing automatically. For best speed, use the same 2.4 GHz network on both devices. A phone on 5 GHz can work when bands share the local network, but some routers introduce long cross-band delays; guest/client isolation can prevent the connection. IP and port are offered automatically through the encrypted paired Bluetooth connection.

Pika opens an authenticated, encrypted local data channel to the phone in the background. Recordings, file synchronization, cloud requests through the phone and voice responses can use this faster path; Bluetooth remains the fallback. The top status identifies the active path as WiFi or BLE. The activity LED follows transfer activity on either transport. Full encrypted backups include the Wi-Fi boost settings and password. Disable the option to keep Bluetooth only.

## Battery calibration
Device & controls → Battery calibration can map a fully charged reading to 4.20 V. Use only at confirmed full charge; the charging LED alone is not a precision voltage measurement. Calibration runs immediately on an awake, idle device and cannot be queued for later. The device applies the saved factor to both voltage and percentage. Reset calibration restores the original formula. Full backups include this correction.

title: Backup, recovery and ownership
markdown:
## Create a complete backup
In Config → Data & recovery choose the complete backup action. Connect Pika first so device settings and mirrored files are available. Choose a password of at least ten characters and confirm it. Save the .pika-backup file somewhere safe; choose Google Drive in Android's document picker for cloud storage when available.

The portable encrypted backup includes records, available WAVs, transcripts, Ask history, phone state and captured device/AI/Google settings. It is independent of the original phone's Android Keystore. The password is required on another phone. Keep both file and password: losing the password makes recovery impossible. Credentials are sensitive even inside an encrypted backup.

## Restore
Choose Restore, select the backup and enter its password. The app validates/decrypts it before replacing the phone library. Confirm applying the restored library to the connected Pika. Keep the phone/app available and the device awake until activation and synchronization finish. Large recordings make a full restore slower than routine sync.

Current device ownership and the current app PIN are retained instead of copied from an old owner. Wrong-password or damaged authenticated backups are rejected. A restore replaces the target library: it is not a merge of two independent libraries. Verify records and connected services afterward. Previous device data may be retained as a recovery copy; do not rely on that as your only backup.

## USB Mount SD
Connect Pika to a computer by USB and use Mount SD in Config while Companion can reach it. The card is exposed read-only for copying. Back up the complete notes folder including hidden files; raw SD copying alone does not include every phone/device setting. Eject the drive on the computer, then use the lower button to leave USB Backup. Never format the mounted card as part of a backup.

## Undo, archive cleanup and reset
Undo last change restores the available previous record state. Archive keeps completed tasks, past events and forgotten memories. Permanent archive cleanup removes retained archived content after confirmation. Factory reset is broader: it clears records, history and device settings. Download and verify a backup before any destructive operation.

## Forget Pika and a new owner
Forget Pika is destructive, not a simple disconnect. It clears device data and settings, removes the binding, clears this app's library and returns to onboarding after confirmation. Back up first. An owned device accepts its bound phone; a new owner pairs after the old owner forgets it. Some Android versions may leave a system Bluetooth entry that must be removed in Android settings.

Unpaired Pika shows its identity and pairing code rather than the library. The short PN serial is useful for choosing the right device. Bluetooth pairing, the app PIN and the encrypted backup password serve different purposes.

## Storage privacy
The current microSD contents are not encrypted at rest. Someone with the card may read its files. Portable complete backups are password-encrypted, but this does not encrypt the installed SD card. USB Mount is read-only access to those files.

title: Troubleshooting
markdown:
## Connected, but changes are still queued
Keep Pika awake and the app available. Check the top status and orange progress line. A connection is not the same as a completed sync. Pull down once to request another attempt. Large WAVs or a full restore take longer; ordinary edits should use incremental exchange. Use Force full sync only when you need a complete verification.

## No connection after wake
Allow a moment for Bluetooth reconnection, check phone Bluetooth and Companion permissions, and make sure another test client is not holding the device connection. Keep the app allowed to run in the background. Saved memories remain queued if the phone is absent. If necessary, use the both-button companion reconnect action from Today.

## Try again / missing transcript
Check phone internet, your AI key and provider availability. Keep an offline recording until recognition finishes. If you manually edited its text, automatic recognition deliberately leaves your changes alone. Open Diagnostics, choose Phone app or Pika SD, and view/download the recent errors. Error journals are bounded, not full audio recordings.

## No sound
Wake and connect Pika, increase volume and choose a sound other than No sound. Test the selected melody from Sound & melody. Notification scenarios have independent patterns. A test command sent while disconnected cannot be heard on the device.

## Calendar or Gmail fails
A saved configuration is not proof of Google access. For Calendar check the explicit ID, calendar sharing with the service-account email and Calendar API. For Gmail check Desktop OAuth credentials, the signed-in account, read-only grant and token expiry. Reconnect the account with the helper when needed. Do not paste keys or tokens into public issues.

## Device recovery
From normal running firmware, hold both buttons for five seconds to request a software restart, even if you keep holding them. This cannot recover ROM bootloader mode or every hard CPU failure. If a USB/serial tool reports a busy port, close the application using it. Use the firmware image for your exact board/display; a color display is not interchangeable with a monochrome driver just because the cable fits.

## Before reporting a problem
Note the firmware/app versions, short device serial, action performed, whether Pika was asleep, phone internet/Bluetooth state and the relevant recent diagnostic entry. Redact personal text and credentials. Back up before trying reset or re-pairing.
